notes: Reached via Chrome connector, no proxy. robots.txt (https://www.castlery.com/robots.txt) has no Claude-specific disallow, only User-agent:* blocking /wishlist,/checkout/,/account/ -- safe to proceed. Castlery is a furniture-first Next.js (App Router) DTC brand; the top nav has explicit departments New/Sofas/Tables/Chairs/Beds/Storage/Furniture Sets/Outdoor/Accessories/Tools/Sale. Tree source: each department's own 'all-X' listing page CATEGORY facet sidebar (the site's own taxonomy, e.g. Sofas -> Sectional/2-seater/3-seater/Modular/Chaise lounges/Footstools-ottomans-poufs/Living room sets), cross-checked against /sg/sitemap.xml (fetched same-origin via javascript_tool, ~1828 URLs) to catch nodes the facet UI didn't surface (found 3-seater-sofas this way; sitemap conversely missed 2 real nodes the facet UI had). Excluded per brief: 'All X' roll-up pages (View-All junk), colour/material/feature/style SEO landing pages that exist in the sitemap under each department (e.g. grey-sofas, boucle-armchairs, l-shape-couch, wood-coffee-tables) -- these are facet re-cuts, not the site's own CATEGORY taxonomy. Mattresses excluded (bedding, not furniture) despite being a CATEGORY facet option under Beds. Outdoor Accessories (/sg/outdoor/outdoor-accessories, 76 items) excluded: inspected in the prior Home-Decor pass on this same site and confirmed to be almost entirely furniture covers (Rio/Sierar *Cover) plus one bar cart -- primary product type of the roll-up is protection/covers (explicit brief exclusion), not furniture, so the whole node is excluded. Duplicate found and dropped: /sg/sofas/chaise-sofas (h1 'Chaise Sofas & Chaise Lounges', numberOfItems=79) is a content-identical alias of /sg/sofas/sectional-sofas (also numberOfItems=79, same first 3 product names in the same order) -- kept only Sectional Sofas, flagged as MANUAL REVIEW on that row for transparency. 'Living Room Sets' (a CATEGORY facet label under both Sofas and Furniture Sets all-X pages) has no live canonical URL: both /sg/sofas/living-room-sets and /sg/furniture-sets/living-room-sets return a blank/generic 'Castlery' page with no h1 and no product JSON-LD (confirmed twice) -- treated as absent, not recorded, per the URL-hierarchy rule (grouping/filter label with no real listing page is not a row). 'Dressers & Chest of Drawers' is cross-listed as a CATEGORY facet under both Beds and Storage departments but resolves to the single canonical URL /sg/beds/dressers in both cases (no separate storage-only dressers page exists in the sitemap) -- recorded once under Bedroom to avoid a duplicate-link row. 'Outdoor Furniture Sets' is a CATEGORY facet under Outdoor but its canonical URL is /sg/furniture-sets/outdoor-sets (confirmed via redirect) -- recorded once under Furniture Sets, not duplicated under Outdoor. No Kids/Nursery furniture line exists on this storefront (sitemap-wide regex for kids|nursery|crib|child returned only a blog post, no product category). Qty method (Rule 1/2): every leaf's qty came from the page's own schema.org ItemList JSON-LD script (<script type=application/ld+json>), field 'numberOfItems' -- this is server-rendered in the initial HTML response (confirmed via network log: the document GET is the only request that returns the listing, there is no separate client XHR/API call feeding the grid, so this is effectively an SSR count, not a client-computed one). Corroborated once independently: on /sg/sofas/sectional-sofas the visible pagination showed '1 2 3 4' pages at 24 products/page (confirmed by counting distinct /products/ hrefs on page 1 = 24), and 24*3+7 = 79 exactly matches the JSON-LD numberOfItems=79 -- confirms the field is an exact per-category product count, not a padded or site-wide total (it changes correctly per category and is not a round/suspicious number). Rendered-header pagination itself was NOT used as the primary qty source because the site's pager is a client-side button (not a real anchor/URL) that proved unreliable to drive programmatically (a direct ?page=N query param is silently ignored and re-serves page 1 -- a confirmed instance of the 'bad param serves the parent/default' trap -- and clicking the pager control via the accessibility-tree ref crashed/froze the render twice), so the JSON-LD field was used directly per Rule 2, which is explicitly permitted when the rendered header is unreliable/unobtainable and is stated here accordingly. h1 was checked against the requested node on every leaf and matched in all cases (no parent-served-under-child-URL instances found here).
